svg.title: Water in a transparent cubic real-space grid
svg.desc: A source-based water molecule with smaller hydrogen display spheres is surrounded by a true four-by-four-by-four Cartesian grid, transparent glass-like faces and soft qualitative positive density contours. No calculated or experimental density data are depicted.
svg.metadata: {"description": "Original scientific editorial illustration of a water molecule in a genuine 4×4×4 real-space grid cube.", "molecule_source": "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Water-3D-balls.png", "molecule_image_url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b4/Water-3D-balls.png", "creator": "Benjah-bmm27 (Ben Mills)", "license": "Public domain, released by creator (PD-user)", "chemical_reference": "https://cccbdb.nist.gov/expgeom2x.asp?casno=7732185", "molecule_integrity": "The verified public-domain source is edited with built-in ImageGen to reduce hydrogen sphere display diameters to about 60%. One oxygen and two hydrogens remain connected by two O-H single bonds. This is an illustrative sphere-size adjustment, not a claim about physical atomic radii; output pixels are no longer the untouched source.", "grid": "A Cartesian cube of 4×4×4 equal cells, orthographically projected isometrically; all 12 projected cube edges are 260 px.", "density": "Teal nested contours and haze are qualitative positive density concepts only. They are not computed water density, signed density, orbital phase, spin density, or measured data.", "editorial_styling": "Glass tints, edge highlights, regular lattice-node glints and soft shadows are decorative rendering, not additional scientific quantities. No nodes are placed off the Cartesian lattice.", "grid_reference": "https://www.octopus-code.org/documentation/main/developers/code_documentation/grids/", "density_reference": "https://goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/E01986", "edited_molecule_sha256": "260d9a611351286849fff9db2af1171f642cdbaefdad95e89583104e8ebb8c63", "image_edit_prompt": "prompts.json: water-hydrogen-display-size"}
